long_biography.plain_text:
For cardiac surgeon Jack Sternlieb, the layout of a hospital was part of patient care. Working with designer Adam Rubinstein, he arranged rooms around a central nursing station so staff could see patients and reach them quickly. His private suites incorporated critical-care equipment, allowing treatment to intensify without moving a patient to another ward.

His research also addressed risks introduced by surgical materials. With colleagues at the Mayo Clinic, he investigated inflammation caused by starch from surgical gloves. He subsequently patented water-soluble coatings for surgical appliances, proposing alternatives that would prevent sticking while avoiding the problems associated with starch.
long_biography.html:
For cardiac surgeon Jack Sternlieb, the layout of a hospital was part of patient care. Working with designer Adam Rubinstein, he arranged rooms around a central nursing station so staff could see patients and reach them quickly. His private suites incorporated critical-care equipment, allowing treatment to intensify without moving a patient to another ward.

His research also addressed risks introduced by surgical materials. With colleagues at the Mayo Clinic, he investigated inflammation caused by starch from surgical gloves. He subsequently patented water-soluble coatings for surgical appliances, proposing alternatives that would prevent sticking while avoiding the problems associated with starch.
